attributes.title: [CVE-2026-66066] Logo upload accepts JPEG-magic-prefixed files, confirming Active Storage arbitrary file read attack surface on GoCardless
attributes.vulnerability_information:
## Summary

The logo upload endpoint at `https://api-sandbox.gocardless.com/logos` performs magic-byte-only content validation. A crafted 22-byte file (JPEG magic bytes + JFIF header + EOI, no actual image payload) was accepted with HTTP 201 and stored verbatim (Content-Length: 22 confirmed by hex dump).

This confirms the attack precondition for CVE-2026-66066 (CVSS 9.5, disclosed 2026-07-29): an attacker with a sandbox merchant account can upload a JPEG-magic-prefixed HDF5 payload that libvips would process during variant generation, reading arbitrary server files including Rails `secret_key_base` leading to RCE.

## Affected Asset

- Endpoint: `POST https://api-sandbox.gocardless.com/logos`
- Frontend: `https://manage-sandbox.gocardless.com/brand/logo-and-colours`
- Component: Rails Active Storage file upload pipeline
- Environment: Sandbox (production assumed equivalent)
- Role required: Authenticated merchant account (no elevated privileges)

## Technical Details

The server validates only the first 4 bytes (magic bytes) of the uploaded file against the declared MIME type. A file beginning with `FF D8 FF E0` (JPEG signature) passes the check regardless of whether the remaining bytes constitute a valid JPEG image.

**Demonstrated with two tests:**

1. File: 22 bytes — JPEG magic bytes (`FF D8 FF E0`) + JFIF header + EOI marker (`FF D9`), no actual image data → **HTTP 201 ACCEPTED**, file stored verbatim
2. File: PNG magic bytes (`89 50 4E 47`) declared as `image/jpeg` → **HTTP 422** `content_type_mismatch`

This proves the server validates only the file header, not its structural integrity. An attacker can prepend JPEG magic bytes to any payload to bypass this check.

**Rails Active Storage + cloud storage backend confirmed:**
- `POST https://manage-sandbox.gocardless.com/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads` accessible, returns GCS XML API error response
- Stored files at `uploads-sandbox.gocardless.com` return `x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256` (S3-compatible backend)
- Rails CSRF confirmed: POST /logos without token → HTTP 422 "Invalid CSRF token", header `x-backend-server: ui`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a GoCardless sandbox merchant account at `manage-sandbox.gocardless.com`
2. Log in and navigate to `https://manage-sandbox.gocardless.com/brand/logo-and-colours`
3. Prepare a 22-byte file with JPEG magic bytes but no valid image payload:
   `FF D8 FF E0 00 10 4A 46 49 46 00 01 01 00 00 01 00 01 00 00 FF D9`
   Save as `poc.jpg` with `Content-Type: image/jpeg`
4. Upload as the organization logo and click "Save changes"
5. Observe: `POST https://api-sandbox.gocardless.com/logos` → **HTTP 201 Created**
6. Fetch the returned `url` → `Content-Length: 22` confirms verbatim storage (no validation)

**Contrast test:** Upload PNG magic bytes (`89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`) declared as `image/jpeg` → HTTP 422 `content_type_mismatch`. Confirms magic-byte check exists but only covers the header.

## Proof of Concept

Run in browser console on `manage-sandbox.gocardless.com/brand/logo-and-colours`:

```javascript
const bytes = new Uint8Array([
  0xFF,0xD8,0xFF,0xE0,0x00,0x10,
  0x4A,0x46,0x49,0x46,0x00,
  0x01,0x01,0x00,
  0x00,0x01,0x00,0x01,0x00,0x00,
  0xFF,0xD9
]);
const file = new File([bytes], 'poc.jpg', {type: 'image/jpeg'});
const dt = new DataTransfer();
dt.items.add(file);
const input = document.querySelector('input[type=file]');
Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype,'files').set.call(input, dt.files);
input.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true}));
// Click "Save changes" → POST /logos → HTTP 201
```

## Observed Result

```
POST https://api-sandbox.gocardless.com/logos → HTTP 201 Created
{
  "logos": {
    "id": "LO01KYSM9BC0RPHGNBVQNCWF5JB7",
    "created_at": "2026-07-30T13:44:10.362Z",
    "url": "https://uploads-sandbox.gocardless.com/57da6f2e0f139e118c7930ae76570491.jpeg"
  }
}

GET https://uploads-sandbox.gocardless.com/57da6f2e0f139e118c7930ae76570491.jpeg
→ HTTP 200 OK | Content-Type: image/jpeg | Content-Length: 22
   Hex: ffd8 ffe0 0010 4a46 4946 0001 0100 0001 0001 0000 ffd9
```

## CVE-2026-66066 Attack Path (NOT tested — policy compliance)

CVE-2026-66066 (CVSS 9.5, disclosed 2026-07-29) affects Rails apps using Active Storage with libvips (default processor since Rails 7.0):

1. Upload file: JPEG magic bytes (`FF D8 FF`) prepended to HDF5 payload with external reference to `/var/app/config/master.key`
2. GoCardless validates magic bytes → **HTTP 201** (upload accepted)
3. GoCardless generates logo thumbnail → libvips processes the file
4. libvips processes HDF5 format, resolves external reference → reads `master.key` from server
5. Attacker signs malicious Marshal payload with `master.key` → **RCE on Rails server**

GoCardless should verify Rails version and patch immediately:
- Rails `< 7.2.3.2` → vulnerable
- Rails `< 8.0.5.1` → vulnerable
- Rails `< 8.1.3.1` → vulnerable

## Recommendations

**Immediate:** Patch Rails to `>= 7.2.3.2` / `>= 8.0.5.1` / `>= 8.1.3.1`. Verify Active Storage image processor version.

**Structural:** Replace magic-byte-only validation with full image decode validation — attempt to decode the file as a valid image at upload time and reject if it fails. Run image processing in a sandboxed environment without filesystem access to Rails secrets or cloud credentials.

**Detection:** Alert on uploads where stored `Content-Length` is below a minimum viable image size (< 100 bytes). Monitor image variant generation errors that include filesystem path information.

## Impact

## Demonstrated Impact

- A crafted 22-byte file (JPEG magic bytes only, no valid image content) was uploaded to `POST /logos` → **HTTP 201 Created**
- File stored verbatim at CDN: Content-Length: 22, hex dump matches exactly the crafted bytes
- Server performs magic-byte validation but only checks the file header, not the full file structure
- This is the exact precondition for CVE-2026-66066: a JPEG-magic-prefixed HDF5 payload would pass this same validation

## Potential Impact (not tested — policy compliance)

If GoCardless runs Rails < 7.2.3.2 / < 8.0.5.1 / < 8.1.3.1 with libvips as the Active Storage image processor:

- **Arbitrary file read** via libvips HDF5 external reference processing during logo thumbnail generation
- **Rails master.key / secret_key_base exposure** — server filesystem files readable by the Rails process
- **Remote Code Execution** via Marshal deserialization after recovering the master.key
- Prerequisite: authenticated sandbox merchant account (low privilege, freely obtainable)

Rails version is hidden behind Cloudflare — patch status cannot be confirmed externally. CVE-2026-66066 was disclosed one day before this report (2026-07-29).
